summary:
I've been working on Switchboard, a FastAPI proxy that serializes access to a single 16GB Tesla P100 across several services that all want the GPU: a local Gemma 26B model, ComfyUI renders, KoboldCPP, and the phillipsben.com site assistant. The model alone occupies nearly the full card, so anything else has to wait. The piece I just finished wiring is a custom ComfyUI node that checks in with Switchboard before a render starts — during testing it acquired the lease in 1.4 seconds, shed the 26B's resident footprint down to 373 MB, and released automatically when the queue drained. One design choice I'm keeping on purpose: the local model waits for in-flight renders rather than being preempted mid-generation. That's the point of having the arbiter.

The project hero images on phillipsben.com are generated through ComfyUI on that same P100, then passed through a duotone step to match the site's color palette before being committed as webp files. I ran two batches to cover fifteen projects. The non-obvious part: line-centric prompts on this checkpoint drift into generic diagonal curves regardless of subject. Dot-field and stipple prompts are far more reliable for getting something that reads as deliberate rather than accidental. Also learned that "message bus" generates a coach bus, and "bounded frame" generates a picture hanging on a wall.

The phillipsben.com site assistant is live — it answers questions about my work using only what's actually published on the site, with a fallback to the local model when the API is busy. I ran 16 adversarial test cases to confirm it can't be steered off the published content before shipping.

I repurposed an ESP32-S3 camera board into a barbell rep counter. It tracks a color-coded weight plate as a fiducial using color-blob detection in HSV — no server, no ML model. The tricky bits were calibration (the crop has to land on the plate center, not background) and a BGR channel ordering issue in the camera library that made the diagnostic readouts show swapped color channels. Cosmetic only, since hue matching is internally consistent, but it cost some time. Validated five out of five reps in a dim room with a blue plate.

BudgetTracker went from dormant to live at budget.phillipsben.com over the past few weeks. A substantial chunk of that was cleaning seven years of imported bank transactions: building transfer detection to pull internal moves and card payments out of the income and expense totals, categorizing what remained, and getting the reported net to something that matched reality. The part that carries forward is a money-movement rule set that runs on every future sync, so new imports classify correctly without a manual cleanup pass each time.

highlights.oneLiner: ComfyUI custom node now acquires the GPU lease from Switchboard before each render
Generated hero images for 15 projects; dot-field prompts outperform line-centric ones on this checkpoint
Career assistant shipped live; passed 16 adversarial tests before release
ESP32-S3 color-blob rep counter validated 5/5 reps; AWB and calibration crop are the tricky bits
